info.name: Himam API
info.description:
API for the Himam reading programme (منصة همم — جمعية مرتقي العلمية).

## Getting started

1. Import the companion environment `Himam-Local.postman_environment.json`, or set `baseUrl` on this collection.
2. Run **Auth → Login (reader)** and **Auth → Login (admin)** once. Their test scripts capture the bearer tokens into `{{token}}` and `{{adminToken}}` automatically — nothing to copy by hand.
3. Everything else is then runnable.

## Language

Every request sends `Accept-Language: {{lang}}` from the collection-level header. Change `lang` to `ar`, `en`, `fr` or `ur` and re-send any request to get the same record back in that language — book titles, quiz questions, badges and notifications are all translated server-side, not just the interface.

Resolution order is `?lang=` → `X-Locale` → `Accept-Language` → the signed-in reader's saved preference. Responses carry `Content-Language`.

## Auth

Laravel Sanctum bearer tokens. Reader routes need `{{token}}`; admin routes need `{{adminToken}}` and an account with `role = admin` (the API returns 403 for a reader, 401 for anonymous).

// Sending Accept keeps Laravel returning JSON for validation and auth
// failures instead of an HTML redirect, and Accept-Language is what makes
// the same request come back translated — flip {{lang}} to ar/en/fr/ur.
// Only supply a default. Overwriting here would silently beat a header
// set on the request itself, which makes a per-request language look
// broken when it is actually being replaced.
// Email is unique, so a fixed address would 422 on the second run.
// Mint a fresh one each time to keep this request re-runnable.
// Set in both scopes: an environment variable of the same name would
// otherwise shadow the collection one and resolve {{token}} to empty.
// Remembered so 'Session end' can delete this account again —
// otherwise every collection run would leave a reader behind.

request.description:
`answers` maps question id → chosen option id.

Grading happens server-side. A pass at or above the configured ratio (60%) credits the section's points, but only the first time — retries after a pass are free to take and earn nothing. The response reports anything newly unlocked in `new_badges` and `new_certificates`.

Run **Get questions** first if you want ids that match your data.
All active badges with an `earned` flag. Locked badges stay visible on purpose — the design greys them out as motivation.
Every certificate the programme can issue, with `earned` and a percent-complete for the ones still ahead. Backs the earned/all tabs on the certificates screen.

The endpoint behind the QR code on every certificate. Public and deliberately minimal — enough to confirm the certificate is genuine, with no contact details. Run **My certificates** first to populate {{verificationCode}}.
`month` and `year` sum the points actually earned inside that window rather than reusing the lifetime total, so a monthly board isn't just a copy of the all-time one.
Broadcasts plus anything addressed to this reader, minus muted categories. Drafts (no `published_at`) never appear.
Opening one marks it read.

Categories: program, exam, results, honor, general.

Set `enabled: false` to mute one — muted categories disappear from the announcements feed entirely. The example uses `true` so a full collection run leaves the demo account's feed intact.
`locale` is the account-level language preference, which follows the reader to any device.

Revokes every other access token, so other sessions must sign in again.

The example deliberately sets the password to its current value: a whole-collection run would otherwise change the demo account's password and lock you out of every later run. Put a real new password in when you actually want to change it.

item.name: Admin
item.description:
Requires {{adminToken}} and an account with role = admin. A reader token returns 403; anonymous returns 401.

Unlike the reader endpoints, these return translatable fields as full `locale => text` maps so the dashboard can offer one input per language.

request.description: Deliberately sends the *reader* token to prove the API enforces the role itself, independently of the dashboard's UI guard.
One language is enough — the rest fall back per field. An entirely empty translatable field is rejected.
Refused with 422 while the level still has books — the cascade would silently void readers' progress.
Omit `position` to append. Paragraphs in `body` are separated by a blank line (\n\n).
A question and its options are saved together — a question with no options is unanswerable. Exactly one option must be `is_correct`, and at least two options are required; anything else is a 422.
Options are replaced wholesale — editing in place would leave stale rows behind when a choice is removed.

Last in the folder on purpose: the requests above create a book, a section and a question, exercise them, then tear them down again — so running this folder leaves your catalogue exactly as it found it.

Includes the reader's stats and their last 20 quiz attempts.

You cannot remove your own admin role — it would lock you out of the dashboard mid-session, so it takes a second administrator.

The example writes back the seeded values so a full run doesn't quietly reshuffle your demo reader.
Re-runs the badge and certificate rules. Useful after content changes — for example when a level gains a book that readers had already completed under the old structure.
Exists so the delete below has something of its own to remove. Deleting a seeded reader would take their attempts, badges and certificates with them.
Point this at {{userId}} to delete a real reader — deliberately not the default. You also cannot delete your own account.

item.name: Session end (run last)
item.description:
Logout revokes {{token}}, so everything after it in a full-collection run would fail with 401. It lives here, at the bottom, so the collection runs cleanly top to bottom.

The cleanup request first removes the account **Auth → Register** created, which is what keeps a whole-collection run from leaving a new reader behind every time.

Revokes the current access token only, leaving other devices signed in. Re-run **Auth → Login (reader)** to get a fresh one.
